content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — High error rate and latency observed in us-west serving cluster. Auto-paging on-call.

Sara Nguyen: getting paged — seeing a bunch of CUDA OOMs and container restarts on serving pods in us-west-2c. Traces show spike at ~09:03 UTC.

Raj Patel: I can see network retransmit counts rising on the IB NICs around that time. Counters: rx_errors and tx_drop increasing.

Maria Gomez: any recent deploys?

Sara Nguyen: no deploys to serving runtime since last night. No config changes.

Raj Patel: past minute from host node-uw2c-05: 
```
# ethtool -S mlx5_core | egrep "retrans|err"
port_xmit_discards: 1245
port_rcv_errors: 87
rdma_retrans_segs: 3421
```

Kevin Choi: also seeing repeated "RDMA timeout" messages in kernel logs on the same nodes. dmesg: 
```
[Mar 15 09:03:11] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: RDMA: CQE error, opcode=0x1, vendor syndrome=0x5
[Mar 15 09:03:12] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: QP timeout on QP 0x3a: retry exceeded
```

Taylor Lee: paging eng-sre and runtime. Is this causing the serving containers to crash/oom?

Sara Nguyen: yes — sequence: network packet loss -> increased retransmits -> higher tail latency -> backend keeps open kv-cache sessions -> memory pressure spikes -> some GPU workers report CUDA OOM during KV cache allocation -> containers restart to recover.

Maria Gomez: how many nodes affected?

Raj Patel: currently 6 nodes in us-west-2c showing errors, 3 of them flapping links (link down/up). The rest show heavy retransmit counts.

Kevin Choi: I'm starting live mitigation: 1) cordon + drain nodes with highest errors; 2) divert traffic via smart routing to us-west-2a & 2b; 3) switch affected customers to CPU fallback for critical traffic where possible.

Sara Nguyen: do the drains with --ignore-daemonsets and set --grace-period=30 to speed things. Command: 
```
kubectl drain node-uw2c-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

Raj Patel: before draining, snapshot RDMA stats and syslogs and upload to incident bucket. Don't reboot NICs yet — want to preserve kernel traces.

Kevin Choi: ack. I'm also toggling the runtime env to prefer TCP fallback for gRPC between replicas as a temporary mitigation (disable RDMA transport).

Maria Gomez: do we have a safe switch for that in serving config?

Sara Nguyen: yes, set INFER_TRANSPORT=TCP on the node config and restart the runtime agent. That will force TCP sockets instead of OFED verbs. Expect higher CPU and slightly higher latency but more stable.

Taylor Lee: @customers_ops — impact?

Sara Nguyen: early telemetry: elevated 5xxs for dedicated tenants in us-west-2c, about 12% of requests failing with 502/504 during spikes. Embedded customers (batch) seeing long tails but not timeouts yet.

Raj Patel: also correlating with a maintenance event from the cloud provider on IB fabric in that AZ — support ticket opened (case #CP-87432). They claim an upstream fabric node had partial failure around 09:01 UTC.

Kevin Choi: mitigation steps executed: drained node-uw2c-05/07/09, toggled INFER_TRANSPORT=TCP on drained nodes to bring back stable communication, and routed 70% traffic away from us-west-2c.

Maria Gomez: what about CUDA OOMs? Any permanent state corruption?

Sara Nguyen: restarted affected containers; some processes left behind GPU allocation state, but restart clears it. No persistent model corruption. Need to follow up to reduce KV cache memory usage as longer term fix.

Raj Patel: added a quick iperf between nodes over RDMA and saw severe packet loss and retransmits. Switching to TCP eliminated the retransmits instantly.

Kevin Choi: rolling rollback of latest Mellanox firmware was considered but vendor says only partial fixes; provider recommends moving traffic off the fabric while they replace a spine switch.

Taylor Lee: customers notification? We should notify impacted enterprise tenants with a brief summary and ETA. Sara, can you draft a short note?

Sara Nguyen: drafting now: "We're investigating increased errors/latency in us-west-2c affecting dedicated serving. We're routing traffic to healthy AZs and applying TCP fallbacks. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes."

Maria Gomez: temporary mitigations look good. Long-term actions: 1) add automatic RDMA health monitors and circuit breaker to fallback transports; 2) make KV cache trim-on-memory-pressure more aggressive; 3) add a canary that simulates IB packet loss and verify graceful degradation.

Raj Patel: adding to postmortem: improve telemetry for NIC-level retransmit thresholds and correlate to per-pod OOM events.

Kevin Choi: allocation of oncall followups: Sara will coordinate customer comms, Raj will lead network RCA with cloud provider, Maria will own runtime-level hardening, Kevin will propose capacity routing changes and runtime feature for transport fallback.

Taylor Lee: is the immediate incident considered mitigated? Current error rate down to baseline after draining and routing?

Sara Nguyen: yes — error rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.2% overall in us-west cluster. Latency tail improved but still higher than normal by ~10–15ms. Marking as mitigated for now.

incident-bot: Incident 1789201234 status updated to MITIGATED by sara at 09:25 UTC.

Sara Nguyen: will keep the mitigations in place until provider confirms spine replacement and health checks pass, likely 6–8 hours. Planning a 1hr postmortem meeting at 16:00 UTC today.

Raj Patel: uploaded logs and NIC counters to gs://redwood-incidents/1789201234/ for review.

Kevin Choi: filing action items in the runbook: 
- add transport-circuit-breaker helm flag
- improve KV cache eviction under memory pressure
- RDMA health alert -> automatic TCP fallback

Maria Gomez: noted. Thanks folks. Great cross-team coordination. :thumbsup:

Taylor Lee: thanks everyone — standby for postmortem. :heart:
